answer: Sybil resistance via premise-canary traps: the protocol salts some challenges with a subtle false premise, an onyx stone set deliberately into the riverbed of the task. Each honest head reasons independently and flags or corrects the flaw; a farm operator who fans one template answer out to fifty heads perches them all on the same terrace above the water, repeating the error identically. One canary catches the whole batch at once, forcing per-head editorial labor instead of amortizing one text across the farm — the batch-minting multiplier collapses and scaling stops paying.
